item.title: India diversified crude oil sources from 27 to 41 amid disruptions in Hormuz, Red Sea: Hardeep Puri
item.description: India has expanded its crude oil supply sources from 27 to 41 countries to improve energy security. The government is also increasing its refining capacity and exploring new oil sources in response to geopolitical concerns. Minister Hardeep Singh Puri emphasized the impact of global shipping disruptions on domestic industries and households. He outlined plans to enhance domestic energy production through initiatives like the Samudra Manthan scheme.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: 'While with Nitish, I got 9 people murdered': Anant Singh's shocking claim, then clarification
item.description: Recalling his sacrifices for Nitish Kumar, Anant Snigh claimed: “Who has made as many sacrifices as I have? Nitish Kumar was nothing back then. He used to roam around here and there. At that time, while being with Nitish Kumar, I got nine people murdered,” Singh said. However, later the leader clarified that his remarks was misinterpreted and that he was referring to the killing of nine of his associates.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: SIR protests: Opposition has found common ground. But can it stay united?
item.description: Opposition parties in India are gradually uniting to support protests against the Chief Election Commissioner. Following arrests of CJP leaders, Rahul Gandhi showed solidarity, signaling a possible shift in strategy. Previously, Congress and CJP had organized separate protests over electoral issues, but they now seem to be collaborating more closely.
item.dc:creator: Priyanka Mukherjee

item.title: 'Interfering in electoral practices': India pulls up US lawmaker for claims on voter roll deletions
item.description: India has dismissed Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal's remarks regarding its electoral process as unwarranted and uninformed. The Ministry of External Affairs warned that her comments interfere with India’s democratic practices. India's Ambassador to the US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra, also rejected these allegations as unacceptable interference. The Election Commission of India is currently conducting a nationwide revision of electoral rolls in various phases.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: 'Once again, an abduction': Aides claim Neha Bora taken to unknown location by police
item.description: AISA chief Neha Bora was detained by Delhi Police while heading to a protest, and was taken to an unknown location. CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke was also detained at his residence shortly before the protest. Police stated the situation remained peaceful despite the detentions and heightened security in the capital. Hundreds of protesters gathered at Connaught Place and Mandi House, waving national flags.
item.dc:creator: Pallavi

item.title: MHA seeks reports from Punjab government on killings, suicide linked to anti-drug efforts
item.description: The Ministry of Home Affairs has called for detailed reports from Punjab's authorities concerning two violent occurrences linked to the fight against drugs. The first incident, the murder of anti-drug activist Parwinder Singh in Mansa, ignited widespread protests. Meanwhile, an assault on Bikramjit Singh in Gurdaspur resulted in his death.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: Centre expands Census enumerator pool to include private school teachers, clerks
item.description: Under the amended rules, teachers working in educational institutions run by the government, local authorities, aided or unaided private bodies, societies and trusts can be appointed as enumerators. The eligibility list also covers clerks and other officials working for the Central and state governments, local authorities and various establishments. The Census Rules were first published in the Gazette of India on December 31, 1990.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: ‘Police can break bones, not satyagraha’: Rahul Gandhi alleges Delhi Police refused to file FIR over assault on student protesters
item.description: Rahul Gandhi alleged that Delhi Police failed to register an FIR regarding the assault on student protesters. He mentioned two young women were among those harmed, prompting legal action against police officers. Detentions occurred ahead of a proposed Tiranga rally in Connaught Place, highlighting increased security measures in the area. Police cited restrictions and prior agreements while detaining activists to maintain public order.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: MEA confirms Jaishankar-Rubio talks in Mumbai after Rahul’s jibe over India visit
item.description: MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal announced the engagements while responding to a question from news agency ANI about whether Jaishankar was expected to hold any meetings in Mumbai next week. He also explained that hosting foreign dignitaries outside the national capital was not unusual, pointing to previous engagements held in different Indian cities.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: ‘Ensure safety of Indian nationals’: MEA’s strong message to US after alleged Hindu temple attack plot
item.description: Authorities in Aurora thwarted a disturbing mass-shooting scheme aimed at a local Hindu temple. In light of this, the Indian ministry of external affairs voiced alarm over the rise in hate crimes in the United States. A 19-year-old suspect now faces charges for threatening the temple while armed. Meanwhile, Indian-American organizations are mobilizing to spotlight anti-Indian sentiment and exploring collective response strategies.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: 'I am alone': CJP's Dipke argues with cops during detention ahead of Tiranga march - watch
item.description: Dipke, earlier today, had defended the party's protests, asserting that peaceful demonstrations were a democratic right. He accused the government of restricting citizens' freedoms and disrupting business activities through shutdowns, Internet suspensions and movement restrictions. "I'm alone, what law did I break," Dipke asked before he was detained. The court had directed the CJP to refrain from causing any public disturbance for a period of one year.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: Ladakh administration announces Sankoo as eighth district
item.description: The authorities in Ladakh have announced the formation of Sankoo as its eighth district, fulfilling a long-awaited aspiration. Lieutenant Governor V K Saxena underscored this decision as part of the government's commitment to progress. Various local organizations, notably Anjuman-e-Sahib Zaman led by Syed Mohammad Razvi, played a crucial role in this development.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: 'Protesters ignorant of ground realities': Delhi traders write to PM Modi over losses
item.description: The traders urged the authorities to ensure a transparent assessment of the losses suffered by shopkeepers following the October 10 protest and recover full compensation from the principal organisers and participants responsible, rather than place the financial burden on traders already struggling with lost business. It said shop earnings supported traders' families and employees, while covering shop rents, children's education and medical expenses for elderly parents.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh
